To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have validated RDTs and proposed a novel approach for the potential use of digitally linked TB diagnostics to facilitate real-time surveillance of RR-TB outbreaks.
we propose a novel approach to facilitate comparison between different TB RDTs used at the same setting to potentially enable real-time detection of TB transmission.
the probe reactions of the three RDTs used to detect RR-TB in the same setting can be used to evaluate transmission of RR-TB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of connected TB diagnostics to facilitate real-time surveillance of RR-TB and to accelerate efforts to achieve global elimination of TB by 2035.
the potential application of digitally linked TB diagnostics for real-time evaluation and control of RR-TB, which may help accelerate progress toward ending TB.
the development of a new approach to facilitate the use of connected TB diagnostics and shared data for RR-TB transmission detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has provided a proof of concept of how to use the data generated by the RDTs for the purpose of outbreak investigation, and this is a first step towards using these data to improve the surveillance system.
this work is a step toward the use of connected diagnostics for real-time evaluation and control of RR-TB.

the proposed approach is a novel approach to potentially detect RR-TB transmission by fully using connected TB diagnostics and shared test results, which is the first pragmatic work to respond to the consensus of TB experts in 2006.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach may be used as an additional tool for RR-TB surveillance, which would complement the existing surveillance system and potentially accelerate efforts to end TB.
the proposed approach can be applied in any setting where multiple RDTs are available.

we have validated and analyzed test results from 3 RDTs, and proposed the potential use of these results in real-time surveillance of RR-TB, which is the first step toward the ultimate goal of eliminating TB through digital connectivity of diagnostics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown how to fully exploit the power of digitally linked TB diagnostics to improve TB care, surveillance, and research.
the potential of connected diagnostics for real-time surveillance of TB transmission is yet to be fully realized.
the use of digitally linked TB diagnostics for real-time surveillance of drug-resistant TB transmission is feasible and can be implemented in the near future.
